output.interpretation: Opening pressure 138 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 2/mm3. Protein 92 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 64 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.68). Gram stain: no organisms. Elevated protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation). Clinical correlation recommended.
AChR binding and MuSK antibodies negative.

Myasthenia_Antibodies.clinical_significance: AChR antibodies are found in most patients with generalised myasthenia gravis and in about half with ocular myasthenia; a negative result does not exclude it. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.reference_range: Improvement of 2 mm or more is positive
findings.result: Left palpebral fissure 6 mm before and 6 mm after 2 minutes of ice application

output.impression: Ice pack test negative: no improvement of the left ptosis after 2 minutes of ice application.

Bedside respiratory function at 4 h: FVC 2.2 L (58% predicted; 30 mL/kg at 74 kg) L. MIP -28 cmH2O L. MEP 52 cmH2O L. Change: FVC 2.4 L to 2.2 L and MIP -32 to -28 cmH2O over 4 h (8% fall in FVC). Cough effective.

output.impression: 24-hour continuous telemetry. Sinus rhythm 64-88 bpm. No pauses and no arrhythmia. Blood pressure 132/80 to 184/106 mmHg with hourly systolic swings of up to 40 mmHg.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week; here severe demyelination with no decrement on repetitive stimulation
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and, with repetitive stimulation, separate it from myasthenia gravis, the mimic the ptosis raises [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infectious and malignant causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR and MuSK antibodies negative; with non-fatigable ptosis, areflexia, sensory loss and no decrement on repetitive stimulation, myasthenia gravis is unlikely
action_criteria.label: Acetylcholine receptor antibodies for myasthenia gravis (unilateral ptosis)
action_criteria.rationale: Unilateral ptosis with limb weakness raises myasthenia gravis; antibodies and repetitive stimulation address it without a pharmacological challenge.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No improvement of the ptosis with ice
action_criteria.label: Optional bedside ice pack test for the ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: A safe bedside test for myasthenic ptosis; it adds little once the ptosis is non-fatigable and repetitive stimulation shows no decrement.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics (potassium, glucose, CK) and give the baseline before IVIg; liver tests and albumin carry prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: He cannot walk at day 5 and is still progressing; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level monitoring and intubation [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 64-88 bpm and labile blood pressure from 132/80 to 184/106 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in severe GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm 76 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 422 ms) and no conduction or repolarisation abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction with IVIg; additive hypotension with plasma exchange is a relative caution only
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check of amlodipine before IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: Amlodipine does not change the choice or the dosing of IVIg or plasma exchange.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].

Do not perform an edrophonium (Tensilon) test: it adds nothing to the negative repetitive stimulation and carries a risk of bradycardia and bronchospasm in a patient with autonomic and respiratory involvement.
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not use succinylcholine if he needs intubation (risk of hyperkalaemia after denervation).
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now: FVC 58% predicted and falling (2.4 to 2.2 L in 4 h) and MIP -28 cmH2O. Repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 2-4 hours with bulbar and cough checks, and intubate electively if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.5 L at 74 kg), MIP or MEP keep worsening, bulbar weakness with weak cough or pooled secretions develops, or respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia appear [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 30 g/day at 74 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because he cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3); plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].

Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses; treat autonomic blood pressure surges only when sustained, with short-acting agents, because of the risk of rebound hypotension [Leonhard_2019].
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while he cannot walk [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.

Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, long-tract signs, a brainstem syndrome). A pupil-sparing ptosis with full eye movements in an areflexic polyradiculoneuropathy does not call for it.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with left ptosis

differential.key_features: Ptosis with limb weakness raises it, but the ptosis is non-fatigable without diurnal variation, reflexes are absent with glove-and-stocking sensory loss, repetitive stimulation shows no decrement, AChR and MuSK antibodies are negative and the NCS is demyelinating.
Pupils are equal with no anisocoria in dim light, so the partial ptosis is not oculosympathetic.

differential.diagnosis: Compressive or microvascular oculomotor nerve palsy
differential.key_features: Eye movements are full and the pupils are spared, so there is neither the pupil involvement of a compressive third nerve palsy nor the extraocular weakness of a microvascular one; isolated levator weakness here is part of the cranial nerve involvement of the polyradiculoneuropathy.
Five-day ascending course, symmetric flaccid limb weakness with global areflexia, glove-and-stocking sensory loss, no long-tract signs, CSF dissociation and demyelinating NCS.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
Symmetric ascending deficits rather than multifocal ones, demyelinating NCS, normal inflammatory markers.

key_clinical_evidence: Ascending four-limb weakness over 5 days with global areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 92 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS: Brighton level 1 once the course plateaus within 4 weeks [Brighton_2011].
Cranial nerve involvement in GBS can be limited and asymmetric, as with this isolated pupil-sparing ptosis; it does not make the case Miller Fisher syndrome or a brainstem process [EAN_PNS_2023].
Areflexia, sensory loss, demyelinating conduction and no decrement on repetitive stimulation separate GBS from myasthenia gravis; an edrophonium challenge is not needed [EAN_PNS_2023].
FVC below 60% predicted with MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O and a falling trend calls for ICU-level monitoring before he deteriorates [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The ptosis is non-fatigable, the pupils are equal and the eye movements full, so it is neither myasthenic, oculosympathetic nor an oculomotor palsy; with global areflexia, sensory loss, CSF albuminocytological dissociation and a demyelinating NCS it is cranial nerve involvement of GBS.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests myasthenia gravis, Horner syndrome, an oculomotor palsy or a brainstem lesion, and marked asymmetry counts against GBS.

interactions: Amlodipine: additive hypotension with the fluid shifts of plasma exchange (relative caution).
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange with amlodipine
general.summary: Interaction review against the recorded medication list (amlodipine 5 mg once daily).

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 76. Normal intervals (QTc 422 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

findings.finding: DML 7.4 ms (markedly prolonged); CV 30 m/s (severely reduced); CMAP 3.2 mV (reduced)
DML 9.8 ms (markedly prolonged); CV 22 m/s (severely reduced); CMAP 1.8 mV (reduced)
Absent bilateral median; absent bilateral peroneal

findings.nerve: Repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz (median-abductor pollicis brevis, facial-nasalis)

findings.finding: Tibialis anterior, vastus lateralis and first dorsal interosseous bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units; no fibrillation potentials or positive sharp waves

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies (median 7.4 ms, peroneal 9.8 ms) with severely reduced conduction velocities (median 30 m/s, peroneal 22 m/s) and reduced CMAP amplitudes. 2. Absent F-waves in median and peroneal nerves; absent H-reflexes. 3. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials. 4. No decrement on 3 Hz repetitive nerve stimulation. 5. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Pattern consistent with a severe demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_description: Unilateral ptosis as the cranial nerve manifestation of GBS closely mimics myasthenia gravis; global areflexia, sensory loss and the NCS refocus the diagnosis on GBS.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required and 2 recommended actions, 1 red herring; a cranial finding that points to the wrong disease and respiratory values at the ICU threshold.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Five days of progressive ascending limb weakness and numbness with a new droop of the left eyelid, without double vision.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. C. is a 57-year-old financial analyst presenting with a 5-day history of progressive bilateral limb weakness and numbness. On day 1 he noted numbness of both hands and feet. By day 2 he had weakness of the toes of both feet. By day 5 the weakness involved proximal and distal muscles of all four limbs and he can no longer walk independently. He has noticed a new partial drooping of the left eyelid without double vision. The droop is present throughout the day, does not worsen with fatigue and does not improve in the morning. He denies any recent respiratory illness, diarrhoeal illness or viral syndrome. He has no dysphagia, dysarthria or shortness of breath. His hypertension had been well controlled on amlodipine.

neurological_exam.additional: No fatigability of the ptosis on sustained upgaze.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact on upper extremities. Lower extremity limited by weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Partial ptosis of the left eyelid; right eyelid normal. Pupils equal and reactive, no anisocoria in dim light. Extraocular movements full in all directions, no diplopia. No facial weakness. No dysarthria. Palatal movement and cough normal.
neurological_exam.gait: Cannot walk independently; requires bilateral support.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric flaccid weakness: hip flexion 4/5, knee extension 3/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 bilaterally. Upper limbs: shoulder abduction 4/5, finger abduction 4/5 bilaterally. No fatigable weakness.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent in all four limbs (biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, knee and ankle). Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Numbness in a glove-and-stocking distribution with mildly reduced pinprick distally. No sensory level.
